requirements.title: IOSTAT_END is assigned for end-of-file without error and is negative
requirements.source: S16.10.2.16 p1; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, physical PDF474.
requirements.definition: IOSTAT_END is the default integer scalar constant assigned to an IOSTAT= variable for an end-of-file condition during input without an error condition, and its value is negative.

pending.iostat-end-assigned-on-endfile-no-error: Open a scratch sequential formatted file, write no records, rewind it, initialize status to 777, execute READ(unit,*,IOSTAT=status) into an integer sentinel, and assert status == IOSTAT_END; mutate the file to contain one record.
pending.iostat-end-negative: Import IOSTAT_END and assert IOSTAT_END < 0 with a separate endfile READ assigning the same named value; mutate the comparison to > 0.

requirements.oracle: Plans are pending and source-derived. Positive plans observe only portable single-image properties fixed by 16.10.2: named-constant type/kind/rank, exact relational properties among ISO_FORTRAN_ENV constants and intrinsic inquiries, successful use of preconnected units, or exact IOSTAT named-constant assignment. Processor-dependent numeric values, module extensions, compiler option/version text, team identity, atomic/event behavior, multi-image preconnection, and message text are not asserted.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Source accounting only. This packet creates no Fortran fixture, compiler invocation, execution evidence, evidence link, fixture approval, oracle approval, or coverage claim. Fixture authors must re-derive every pending plan from the pinned source. Existing tests and profiles mention ISO_FORTRAN_ENV, CHARACTER_KINDS, INTEGER_KINDS, COMPILER_VERSION text in a test name, and unrelated INT8-style identifiers; this packet records that coverage without rebinding it. The numeric IOSTAT_END value beyond negativity is not asserted.
